records.question: The settlement: where does the cash finally settle, and in what kind of money?
records.answer: In most of what the library holds, the cash still settles in money that already existed. Swift's ledger coordinates commitments among 17 listed banks, 8 of which have a completed pairing located; final settlement happens afterwards through existing payment systems. Of the 12 market systems, 1 settles in central-bank money by the master's own description (Sterling Fnality Payment System), 4 move banks' own tokenized deposits, and for 7 the master does not say. Who finances the interval before settlement: banks validated funding and managed the interval before external settlement. Customer availability can precede bank cash receipt.

records.question: Failure and remedy: when it breaks, who can freeze, who pays, who decides?
records.answer: For 18 of the 36 crypto dollars the library tracks, the issuer can freeze or block coins; for 15 the terms read do not say. When a firm collapsed, customers were being paid back at least partly in 3 of the 10 cases on the International Crypto Map, and courts decided whether customer crypto was the customer's property or the estate's. The 7 programmable-payment failures were corrected by forks, freezes or restitution, not one rule. 37 of 41 U.S. jurisdictions in the register have enacted UCC Article 12, the law on who owns a controllable electronic record.

records.question: The world: how do the other jurisdictions do it?
records.answer: The International Crypto Map reads 22 jurisdictions on 13 dimensions each, from who has authority to who bears a loss; 191 of the 286 cells are researched, 85 partial and 10 still open. 7 of its 14 issuer records are live under a local license, 15 cross-border routes were reviewed and none is yet a recurring end-to-end corridor in the record, and most systems still finish in an existing bank or central-bank record.

records.question: The watch: what is dated, overdue, or still unknown?
records.answer: The crypto library holds 396 dated items and 308 undated clocks and open questions. 2 are past due with no record: Singapore: Stablecoin legislative consultation closes (2026-10-16); Did Treasury submit Scott Bessent's written answers from the September 15 HFSC hearing… (2026-10-20). 14 dates fall in the next 30 days: What first authoritative objects move either ARK's Exchange Class or Tokenized Class from… (2026-10-23); What does the Supreme Court do with Custodia Bank's certiorari petition in No. 26-62, and… (2026-10-28); Australia: RITS consultation closes (2026-10-30).

records.question: When a shop "accepts stablecoins," what does the shop actually receive?
records.answer: A shop can accept a customer's stablecoin payment and still receive ordinary money. The saved Stripe product credits the merchant in USD, while Shopify defaults to its normal payout currency and lets eligible merchants claim USDC instead. Stablecoin-funded cards also pay shops through ordinary card settlement. Separately, some processors offer stablecoin settlement after shoppers pay normally. The saved records mix live products, limited offerings, pilots and infrastructure; they do not show how most shops are paid.

records.question: MKUltra: what did the June 30, 2026 hearing establish, and what is still open?
records.answer: On June 30, 2026 the House Oversight Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets (chair Rep. Anna Paulina Luna) heard Stephen Kinzer (book: Poisoner in Chief), Tom O'Neill (book: Chaos), Dr. Elizabeth Ginexi (former NIH) on MKUltra. It is a declassification and oversight hearing, not a prosecution, and made no legal finding. The chair committed on the record to contact the German government about Camp King and Villa Schuster. All 5 follow-ups have no recorded status since June 30, 2026, and only 1 of 5 cited sources is primary.

records.question: Which tracked crypto dollars are excluded, likely outside, unresolved or wound down?
records.answer: Of these 19 saved entries, six are deposits or securities excluded by the Act’s text; eight are assessed by the Library as likely outside the definition, without a regulator ruling; three remain unresolved or issuer-dependent; and two are wound down. Each card keeps its own evidence date.

records.question: Which shared bottlenecks do several NSSTS programs depend on, and which are overdue for a check?
records.answer: 15 shared bottlenecks sit under the NSSTS programs; the widest, OTA and consortium prototype-to-production transition, touches 6 sectors and 19 company positions, and 6 of the 15 are past their check date with no newer check on record.

records.question: Could the public record have predicted the 2026 NSSTS winners?
records.answer: Only partly: in 4 decisions made between February 10, 2026 and July 9, 2026, the public record named the serious field beforehand in 2 (for example 5 contenders, 2 picked), but the package rates 1 case strong and 3 partial, and in none could it single out the winners.

records.question: Which exact legal company holds each NSSTS role, and who owns it?
records.answer: The NSSTS registries name 16 legal entities that recur across sectors: 9 are subsidiaries held by a larger company (for example Amazon Web Services, Inc., owned by Amazon.com, Inc.), 3 are top companies, and for 4 the registries record no owner; 1 acquired company is still listed on its own and is shown here under its owner.

records.question: Which NSSTS company positions are confirmed, which are educated guesses, and which have evidence against them?
records.answer: Of the 182 company positions on the NSSTS map, 139 are labelled confirmed, 42 are educated guesses (28 strong inference, 13 supported inference, 1 plausible fit) and 1 is blocked or contradicted; 39 positions cite evidence against themselves, 33 of them still labelled confirmed.

records.question: If one NSSTS program fails, what else breaks, and what are the warning signs?
records.answer: The package traces 18 failure chains; the widest (“A transformer factory delay, failed FITT field test, or unaccepted transformer delivery constrains a major project interconnection”) reaches 5 sectors. 15 of the 18 are rated high immediacy, and 2 are past their re-check date with no newer check.

records.question: Which dated decisions in the next year will show whether each NSSTS company's position is real?
records.answer: 34 dated decisions across 12 companies run from August 27, 2026 to December 31, 2027; 2 have passed with no recorded outcome, and the next is due October 31, 2026 (BAE Systems Information and Electronic Systems Integration Inc.).
